objections.explanation: The stated proposition is only that a, b, and c are nonintegers, and its proof of that proposition is sound: with reduced coprime m,n, opposite parity makes H,D and both numerator factors of b odd, yielding v2(a)=v2(b)=-3; when m,n are both odd, v2(H)=1, v2(D)≥3, and the two b numerator factors are 2 and 6 modulo 8, yielding v2(a)=1-3-v2(D)<0 and v2(b)=-3v2(D)<0. Since m,n are nonzero and D≠0, 0<|D|<H, so 0<|c|<8/9. There is no mathematical defect in this three-coordinate argument. However, the frozen author output also declares the broader all-six family assertion and the main existence questions unresolved. Under the supplied controller instruction, a review cannot silently erase those declared gaps or pass this frozen candidate.

confirmed_fragments.claim: For every rational t outside {0,1,-1}, the first three supplied coordinates a,b,c are nonintegers.
confirmed_fragments.audit: Writing t=m/n in lowest terms gives nonzero m,n and D≠0. If m,n have opposite parity, H,D,m²−7n², and 7m²−n² are odd, so v2(a)=v2(b)=−3. If both are odd, v2(H)=1, v2(D)≥3, and the two b numerator factors are respectively 2 and 6 modulo 8, hence each has valuation exactly 1 and is nonzero. Thus v2(a)=1−3−v2(D)<0 and v2(b)=−3v2(D)<0. Finally, H±D=2m²,2n²>0 implies 0<|D|<H, so 0<|c|=(8/9)(|D|/H)^3<8/9. These establish the stated three-coordinate claim for every parameter in its domain.
